docTitle: ConsentKit — cookie consent banner for your site
docDesc: A cookie consent banner you can install in ten minutes. It asks your visitors before any tracker starts. 34 languages, Google Consent Mode v2, a cookie scanner and a consent log. Open source, MIT.
heroTitle: A cookie consent banner you can install in ten minutes
heroLine1: Most banners only draw the buttons. On those sites the trackers start straight away, whatever the visitor presses. EU rules require otherwise.
heroLine2: ConsentKit asks your visitor first and starts the trackers and ads only afterwards. It speaks 34 languages on its own and records every answer, so you have something to show if you are ever asked.
heroNote: Free forever: one site, all 34 languages, one manual scan per day.

how1Text: Copy one line from the dashboard and paste it at the top of your site. It works on Tilda, WordPress and any other site.
how2Text: The dashboard visits your site and checks the line is there. That also proves the site is yours.
how3Text: We walk your pages and find every tracker and cookie you are running. You get back a ready-made list for the banner.
how4Text: The banner already works and the first cookie list publishes itself. After that you can change the colours and wording to match your site.
feat1Title: Trackers stay quiet until the answer
feat1Text: Almost every tracker and ad stays off until your visitor presses a button. That is exactly what the rules require, and exactly what decorative banners never do. The rare exceptions are found for you, with instructions on what to fix.
feat2Text: You do not have to remember what is running on your site. We walk the pages, find every tracker and cookie, and write the list for the banner.
feat3Text: If anyone asks how you can prove consent, the answer is already saved. We record the time and what the visitor chose, and on paid plans you can download the whole log as a file.
feat4Text: Visitors see the banner in their own language and you translate nothing. Leave it as it is, or write your own wording.
feat5Text: A refusal does not switch your advertising off completely: Google still gets a proper signal and keeps counting, just without personal data. There is nothing for you to set up.
feat6Text: It installs on whatever your site is built with. WordPress has a plugin, and everything else takes one line you can paste even on free Tilda.
priceLede: A plan covers your organisation, not a single site. Moving to a cheaper plan never breaks anything: the banner keeps working, automatic scans stop, and the attribution line comes back.

faq: What is cookie consent and why is it needed?

A cookie is a small note a site leaves in your visitor’s browser. Under EU rules anything not needed to run the site itself may only start after the visitor agrees, and you have to be able to prove they did. ConsentKit asks, waits for the answer and saves the decision for you.
Does ConsentKit really block everything before consent?

Almost everything, straight away: the official Google Analytics, Metrica, Meta, TikTok and Hotjar codes are stopped automatically, and Google receives Consent Mode v2 signals before any tag loads. Less common are trackers written into the page by hand, which the browser starts fetching first, so those spots need marking once. The dashboard shows you exactly which ones and what to do.
On servers in Lithuania, that is, in the European Union. The company is European too: E-COM CONSULT PLUS. We store the fact of consent and what the person chose, not information about the visitor.
Can I use it without the dashboard?

Yes, and free of charge. The software is open under the MIT licence: download the files, put them on your site and set it up by hand, with no sign-up. The dashboard is for people who would rather press buttons than edit files.
How do I turn off the “Made by E-COM Consult” line?

On paid plans a switch in the site settings turns it off; on the free plan it stays. If you installed the banner yourself, without the dashboard, you can remove the line in your own copy’s settings. We charge for the dashboard, the scans and keeping the log, not for hiding a line.
What about scanning sites that are not mine?

You may only scan your own sites, or client sites you have been asked to look after. That is why a site has to be verified in the dashboard before the first scan. The scanner treads lightly and does not put load on your site.
